newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico says Zapatista trip would end talks.
newsitem.headline: Mexico says Zapatista trip would end talks.

text.p: Mexico's chief government negotiator for peace talks with Zapatista rebels on Friday said talks would be broken off if rebels left their jungle strongholds in southern Chiapas state for a reported weekend trip to Mexico City.
"It would be a provocation to the government and would imply a breaking of the law," Marco Antonio Bernal told Mexico City's Radio Red radio station.

Organizers of an indigenous congress in Mexico City due to start next week have said that some rebel leaders plan to leave the Chiapas jungle this weekend to travel in a bus convoy escorted by supporters to Mexico City.
The Zapatistas themselves have not given a clear indication about whether they or their charismatic leader, Subcommander Marcos, plan to make the journey.
The government has suspended arrest orders on Zapatista leaders while it tries to negotiate peace. Talks have dragged on and off since the rebels launched their rebellion in 1994.

"If the law is broken, we return to a previous legal status of the Zapatistas, where they are a group that has declared war on the Mexican government, that is clandestine and posseses illegal weapons. That implies a lot of crimes," Bernal said, adding that any Zapatistas who left Chiapas would be subject to arrest.
